newsitem.title: USA: Actress who was voice of Snow White is dead at 80.
newsitem.headline: Actress who was voice of Snow White is dead at 80.

text.p: Adriana Caselotti, who earned a place in animated film history as the voice of the Walt Disney cartoon character Snow White, has died.
Walt Disney Co. said on Monday that Caselotti died on Sunday at her home in Los Angeles following a bout with cancer. She was 80 years old.
Her former husband, Florian St. Pierre, and a close family friend, Gary Stark, were with Caselotti when she died, Walt Disney said in a statement.

Caselotti was cast in the lead vocal role in "Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs" 60 years ago after a Walt Disney casting agent contacted her father, a well-known voice coach. More than 150 young women had already auditioned for the part but none had provided the "ageless, friendly, natural and innocent" voice Disney was seeking.
Listening in on her father's conversation, the younger Caselotti chimed in, "Wouldn't my voice do?"

After making the film, she remained active in publicity activities surrounding its many reissues, and continued to entertain her fans by singing such songs as "Some Day My Prince Will Come" and "Whistle While You Work."

Born into a musical family in Bridgeport, Connecticut, Caselotti was educated at an Italian convent near Rome while her mother was singing at the Opera. Along with the role of Snow White, she made radio guest appearances in New York and Hollywood and had bit parts in several movies including "The Wizard of Oz."
